newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai short-term rates seen falling as inflows up.
newsitem.headline: Thai short-term rates seen falling as inflows up.

text.p: Bank of Thailand deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulsawat said on Monday local short-term interest rates would tend to be lower as a steady return of foreign fund inflows helped ease liquidity.
Chaiyawat said the foreign investors had returned to invest in Thailand this year because of attractive local interest rates and rising confidence in the economy.
"There has been steady inflow of foreign funds recently compared with the heavy outflow late last year," Chaiyawat told reporters.
"If the liquidity stayed at this level, the short-term interest rates are likely to go lower," he said.
Dealers said the inflow of foreign funds since early this year had helped stem the baht's weakness against the rising dollar over the past few weeks.
Selling of the dollars against baht had prompted the U.S. unit to be traded at a relatively lower level against the central bank's fixing, dealers said.
But the high demand for funds to meet the BOT's reserve requirement this week pushed the overnight interbank rate up sharply on Monday, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 12.00-12.50 percent in late trade compared with 11.50-12.00 in the morning and 10.50-10.75 late on Friday.
Chaiyawat said the central bank would attempt to hinder high volatity in short-term interest rates by implementing new measures, if necessary, to mop up excess liquidity.
He did not give detail any of the planned new measures.
